headline: A noodle-cooking robot at a South Korean highway rest stop dropped a block of ramen and flashed a "Failure" alert, and the photo went viral.
score_reason: Pool score 2 lowered by 1: the incident dates from the week before 6 Oct and is a minor glitch.
importance_line: Travelers at the rest stop got a refund and a laugh, while the wider point is that cooking robots are spreading fast in jobs hard to staff at night; the glitch was reported as rare.
summary: SBS News reports that a photo of a ramen robot's red "Failure" alert, taken after it dropped a noodle block at the Gapyeong Service Area on South Korea's Seoul-Yangyang Expressway, went viral last week. The robot's developer says such failures are rare and customers get a refund, and the article notes that service-area cooking robots grew from 3 stores in 2021 to 103 last year.
notes: Incident is from the week before 6 Oct 2026, exact date not given; summary says so. SBS page is an AI translation of a Korean report; photo credited to Ruliweb and Yonhap News.
